findings.title: Separate pending mutation proof from ordinary CI builds
findings.section: Verification Contract — Baseline and platform obligations
findings.why_it_matters: Successful ordinary PR CI cannot discharge R3 (caught-mutation proof) for the Linux-only repairs. The workflow builds the clean head through check-shards and vm-checks, but never applies the isolated mutants required by this plan; with no local Linux builder, those obligations remain outstanding even after every listed CI job passes. Explicitly assigning their supported-builder execution and keeping them in the readiness evidence prevents an incomplete audit cutover from being called ready.
findings.suggested_fix: Assign the parent evidence integrator responsibility for obtaining a supported Linux/KVM execution route for outstanding isolated mutation rounds after publication, and state that ordinary clean-head CI results satisfy only control/build evidence. Keep each unsupported mutation round separately pending and require its intended failure plus restored control before readiness; builder unavailability remains no barrier to implementation or initial publication.
evidence: Each repair register row has an owner assertion, a passing unmutated control and a deliberately broken control that fails for its intended reason (R3).
Implementation and PR publication may proceed after supported local gates, with each unavailable Linux, architecture and VM result explicitly pending for CI.
Merge readiness requires successful current-head PR workflow evidence, all declared checks, VM tests and every production/bootstrap output under the repository policy (R6).
